items.title: cell datum dominance and cell ideals
items.scaffold_contract: Define a finite poset, basis C_st^λ, anti-involution *, and the coefficient-independence axiom modulo the higher-cell span. Prove the higher-cell span is a two-sided ideal from this axiom before forming quotients. Give multipartition dominance and row-standard tλ explicitly.

items.title: The cyclotomic anti-involution fixes the affine and Murphy generators
cyclotomic murphy elements
items.scaffold_contract: For a_c=Σ_(b<c)|λ^(b)| set u_λ=∏_(c=2)^r∏_(i=1)^a_c(L_i−u_c) and x_λ=Σ_(w∈S_λ)T_w, with S_λ the rows of the initial standard multitableau. Prove x_λu_λ=u_λx_λ. Set m_λ=u_λx_λ and m_st=T_(d(s))^*m_λT_(d(t)), where d(t) sends the initial tableau to t and * fixes T_i,L_i. These are genuine elements before any basis/cellularity claim; no omitted parameter rescaling is allowed.

items.title: Integral type-A Garnir straightening and the Murphy cell law
items.scaffold_contract: The local proof establishes the integral standard Murphy basis, Garnir straightening, and lexicographic cell law. The required dominance upgrade follows the plan route: the universal row-eigenvalue equations propagate a nonzero coefficient across adjacent incomparable swaps within each row-label block; if a block contains two boxes in one column, a vertical cover pair can be consecutive in a block extension, contradicting the column eigenvalue -1 versus Q. The source Proposition 3.16 coefficient-elimination argument has an unresolved same-row case in its maximal-term subtraction. Do not mark the dominance ideals or dominance cell law ready until a complete local horizontal-strip support proof is supplied. The unresolved result is an integral type-A supplier used by componentwise straightening, component-shift ideals, and cyclotomic cellularity.

items.title: Componentwise initial-row straightening
items.scaffold_contract: For multicompositions, decompose row-standard tableaux into initial-kind tableaux and distinguished component coset representatives. Apply the ordinary type-A composition-to-partition straightening component by component; prove the row-prefix inequalities, then show each coset relabeling sends a global cutoff to an initial segment in every component interval. Record the ordinary type-A dominance supplier as open until its horizontal-strip support argument is completed. Do not infer acceptance from this planned interface.

items.title: Cyclotomic component shift and multipartition dominance ideals
items.scaffold_contract: For u_a=prod_c prod_{j<=a_c}(L_j-u_c), prove the Q^{a_k} component-shift identity directly from the affine recursion; multiply by the inverse finite T word to separate the u_a and u_b terms. Decompose a tableau permutation into component and component-coset factors. At k=1 use the cyclotomic polynomial; at k>1 use the row-coset sum that moves one box from component k to a new final row in component k-1. Give all dominance-prefix counts and use the componentwise straightening interface to close on X_1. This consumer remains escalated while that interface is unresolved.

items.title: The cyclotomic Murphy basis and cellularity
items.scaffold_contract: Use the ordinary type-A, componentwise, and component-shift suppliers to prove the dominance cell law and ideal closure, then prove spanning from the all-singleton last-component Murphy element. The colored RSK count equals the integral Ariki-Koike PBW rank; the square spanning matrix has a right inverse and is therefore a basis. The present theorem proof is conditional on the unresolved type-A dominance refinement and must be escalated until that supplier is complete.

items.title: Cell modules, their forms, and radicals
items.scaffold_contract: For an arbitrary cellular algebra over a commutative ring, construct the free cell module from coefficient matrices; prove its module law by quotient associativity; derive the unique product form from the left and right coefficient laws; prove symmetry, involution invariance, and radical stability. This abstract result does not use the cyclotomic basis theorem as a premise.

items.title: Nonzero cellular heads classify the simple modules over a field
items.scaffold_contract: For a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field, prove the rank-one action identity, absolute simplicity by scalar extension, a Hom-order obstruction, pairwise distinction, and completeness using a finite maximal-first filtration by cell ideals. No categorification or unproved supplier is used.
